blocks.text: Generally, the freshwater animals are hypertonic to their environment. It means that they have higher solute concentration in body fluids than the surrounding water. Water continuously enters their bodies through osmosis, particularly across permeable surfaces like gills. Essential salts and ions (like Na⁺ and Cl⁻) diffuse out of the body into the surrounding water.

In osmoregulation, they prevent water from entering their bodies and eliminate the excess water that does enter. For this purpose, they produce large volumes of diluted urine. To compensate the loss of salts, they actively transport salts back into their bodies. Unlike their marine water animals, freshwater animals rarely drink water.
